purpose: Dalfampridine is used to help improve walking in adults with multiple sclerosis (MS). It does not cure MS, but it can help your legs work better so you can walk faster and more steadily. It has been shown to help some people with MS feel more stable on their feet.
how_it_works: In MS, the nerves in your body can lose their protective coating, which makes it hard for signals to travel properly from your brain to your muscles. Dalfampridine works by blocking tiny channels on the nerve cells called potassium channels, which helps the electrical signals travel more effectively along damaged nerves. Think of it like helping a weak electrical wire carry its signal better so your muscles get the message to move.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include urinary tract infections (UTIs), trouble sleeping, dizziness, headache, nausea, weakness, and back pain. You may also feel a tingling or burning sensation, especially in your hands or feet.
warnings: This medication can cause seizures, which is the most serious risk — especially if you take more than prescribed or if you have kidney problems. Do not take more than two tablets per day and space them about 12 hours apart. Tell your doctor right away if you have a seizure or feel unusual neurological symptoms. This drug should not be used if you have a history of seizures or moderate to severe kidney disease. Also, do not take other forms of 4-aminopyridine (4-AP) while using this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 10 mg tablet taken by mouth twice a day, about 12 hours apart (for example, morning and evening). Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or break it. Take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same times each day to keep a steady level in your body.
